body: Sometimes creative people go to the well once too often, so that a movie based on a show may feel a little stale, but that wasn't the case here. This one picked up right where Matt Johnson and Jay McCarrol left off, and while it started with the same idea, the maniacal pursuit of landing a gig at the Rivoli, it quickly got into its own intricate plot. It's a very clever film and I enjoyed it from beginning to end. I'll be vague on purpose to avoid spoiling anything, but to provide a little taste, some of the highlights included alternate timelines, Matt and Jay having very different motivations, and things that happen in the RV and on the CN Tower. As always, including real bystanders on the streets of Toronto made me smile, and the fellas also integrated some footage of themselves from the web series circa 2008, which was fun and well done. There were several times when I wondered how they had done something, and it would be great to see Nirvana the Band the Show the Movie the Documentary explaining it. It's also a film with heart at the center of all its zaniness. Great stuff.

Watched at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival.

Safe to say, Matt Johnson has become one of the best Canadian filmmakers in our current times. Johnson has crafted a hilarious and excellent buddy comedy sci-fi movie that clearly understands the self-awareness motions the setting plays, and crafting many creative humorous choices and decisions that are perfect. With a very low budget, what I love about Johnson's work is that Johnson always finds creative ways to tell his stories, direction, and choices in unique ways even when the money is low. His creative approach on the setting, atmosphere, themes, and tone are absolutely brilliant.

Throughout of this movie, based on his web series, this movie successfully captures the insanity and hilarious moments as the show did, adding with new commentaries, fun characters, and humor all around. Matt Johnson and Jay McCarrol as the main duo continues to have strong chemistry, fun dialogue, and entertaining moments together, as they are one of the best Canadian duos of comedy era. Alongside with some very creative editing choices, camerawork, and music choices.

The writing takes clever notes and takes on blockbusters but also new creative concepts and themes that really work. I must say it's quite risky but there are certain moments that I am surprised copyright has been striked yet cause wow, Johnson doesn't hold back the punches.

The TIFF experience I attended was a blast. Everyone was laughing, cheering, and going insane over the movie. It's one of the best Midnight Madness experiences I have seen in my life.

Overall, this was one of the best movies I have seen at TIFF, and frankly, one of the best of this year.

Canada is here to dictate the cultural zeitgeist in TV and movie with Heated Rivalry and this brilliant, beautiful, hilarious, and chaotic masterpiece, respectively.

I haven't laughed this hard in a long time at a movie. They walked a razor thin wire between zany and brilliant, and we owe these guys a great debt for it.

It was hilarious, touching, and insane all at the same time. The fact that they shot parts of the movie 17 years ago is bewildering to me. Their guerrilla-style of filmmaking is truly remarkable to see. Using an actual shooting at Drake's mansion to get shots for this movie was astonishingly genius.

I doubt I'll see a movie like this one again. It's lightning in a bottle.

Saw this at Monday Mystery movie night. Some folks walked out but those of us who stayed experienced a truly original comedy full of surprises and edge-of-your-seat suspense! I've never heard of Nirvana the Band but this indy gem was well worth the wackiness! Even on the small screen, it's a departure from the everyday trite that's out there. If you want a unique quirky laugh for 90 mins, go for it! Grab a bottle of Orbitz and enjoy!

By far the funniest movie I have seen this year, and I have seen a lot! It was a pleasure to watch this in a sold out theater, the jokes did not stop rolling the entire way through. I knew of the web series which were nice short episodes and didn't know how this would translate onto the big screen, but this is such a strong performance. Everything about the movie feels organically driven, I could not stop laughing. Best is in the middle of it all there is a heart felt connection between these two characters and even if you have never seen the show or web series before you will feel that warmth as well. One of my favorites of the year.
